posts.title: Ferroelectric Tuning Reduces Optical-Interconnect Stalls In LLM Training (Georgia Tech)
posts.summary:
Researchers from Georgia Institute of Technology published a technical paper titled “Thermal Tuning Overhead in Wafer-Scale Optical Interconnects for LLM MoE Training: A Cross-Layer Analysis and Ferroelectric-Based Mitigation.” Abstract Excerpt: The paper analyzes “wafer-scale optical interconnects” for mixture-of-experts LLM training and finds “repeated tuning stalls during communication phases.” It also reports “speedups of 2.7x” for... » read more
The post Ferroelectric Tuning Reduces Optical-Interconnect Stalls In LLM Training (Georgia Tech) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Georgia Tech researchers identified that thermal tuning overhead in wafer-scale optical interconnects causes significant communication stalls during the training of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs.
The study proposes a ferroelectric-based mitigation strategy to address these bottlenecks, which currently hinder the efficiency of large-scale AI training clusters.
Experimental results demonstrate a 2.7x speedup for the Mixtral 8x7B model when these specific tuning stalls are effectively eliminated.
This finding is highly relevant for data center infrastructure, as optical interconnects are increasingly vital for scaling high-performance computing and AI workloads.

posts.title: Rowhammer Backdoor Injection Attack During Inference (Northeastern)
posts.summary:
Researchers from Northeastern University published a technical paper titled “ROBBIN: Rowhammer-Based Backdoor Injection during Inference.” Abstract excerpt: “This work presents ROBBIN, a hardware-aware Rowhammer-based backdoor injection attack that integrates the device-specific vulnerability into the backdoor construction process. ROBBIN first characterizes the bit-flip patterns of a target DRAM and uses this information to iteratively select DRAM... » read more
The post Rowhammer Backdoor Injection Attack During Inference (Northeastern) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers at Northeastern University have developed ROBBIN, a novel hardware-aware attack that utilizes Rowhammer-induced bit-flips to inject backdoors into AI models during inference.
Unlike previous hardware-agnostic methods, ROBBIN characterizes specific DRAM bit-flip patterns to iteratively map model weights, ensuring the backdoor remains robust across different devices.
The attack is designed to maximize the Attack Success Rate (ASR) while maintaining the Target Accuracy (TA) of the model, posing a significant security risk for deployed AI systems.
This research highlights a critical vulnerability in the physical layer of DRAM, suggesting that hardware-level security must be integrated into the AI model deployment lifecycle.

posts.title: Generative Design Optimizes Liquid-Cooling Channels For 2.5D And 3D Packages (UM-Dearborn)
posts.summary:
Researchers from University of Michigan-Dearborn published a technical paper titled “Generative Design of Liquid-Cooling Channels for Thermal Management of 2.5D and 3D Integrated Advanced Packaging.” Abstract Excerpt: The paper presents “a physics-guided generative design framework for liquid cooling channel topology optimization” in a “2.7 kW multi-chip package containing two high power GPUs and one CPU.”... » read more
The post Generative Design Optimizes Liquid-Cooling Channels For 2.5D And 3D Packages (UM-Dearborn) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: University of Michigan-Dearborn researchers introduced a physics-guided generative design framework to optimize liquid-cooling channel topologies for advanced 2.5D and 3D integrated packages.
Testing on a 2.7 kW multi-chip package containing two GPUs and one CPU showed a 33.6% reduction in maximum GPU temperature.
The design optimization also achieved a 52.5% improvement in temperature spread and a 72.8% reduction in pressure drop, significantly enhancing thermal management efficiency.
As AI chips continue to increase in power density, these generative design techniques provide a scalable path for cooling high-performance heterogeneous integrated circuits.

posts.title: FAW-VW opens ID. AURA T6 pre-sales, betting on locally developed smart tech to win over Chinese buyers
posts.summary:
The ID. AURA T6 starts at a pre-sales price of 135,900 yuan ($20,040) and offers a range of up to 660 km.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: FAW-Volkswagen has launched pre-sales for the ID. AURA T6, a mid-size SUV priced between 135,900 and 169,900 yuan, marking the debut of its new AURA lineup.

The vehicle is built on the CEA architecture, a joint development between Volkswagen and Xpeng, which utilizes a central computing and zonal control design to support advanced OTA updates and AI model deployment.

Volkswagen is aggressively integrating local Chinese technology, utilizing Horizon Robotics' Journey 6H chip for urban NOA capabilities and featuring LiDAR on higher-end variants for the first time in an all-electric VW SUV.

The T6 offers two battery configurations providing up to 660 km of CLTC range, signaling a strategic shift to compete directly with domestic Chinese smart EV brands through localized hardware and software partnerships.

posts.title: Autonomy and Innovation
posts.summary: Incentives favor offense when it comes to agentic cybersecurity; it's the same dynamic that will limit incumbents and fuel startups in the long run.
bullets: The distinction between 'white hat' and 'black hat' hackers is defined by intent and incentives rather than technical capability, as both groups utilize the same fundamental skillsets to exploit or patch vulnerabilities.
In the context of AI, the proliferation of powerful, widely available models means that cybersecurity threats are no longer restricted to a single entity or nation-state.

Attempting to restrict access to advanced AI models is a flawed strategy because the best defense against AI-driven cyberattacks requires that defenders have equal or superior access to the same powerful models.

The author argues that government-led efforts to centralize AI control, such as the response to Anthropic's Fable release, are counterproductive and ignore the reality of a decentralized, global AI landscape.
